cards.title: Session-per-pane grid sized by pane count
cards.user_does: Asks for more or fewer sessions in a workspace.
cards.user_sees: The terminal grid grows or shrinks between 1 and 12 panes, each pane its own session.
rules: Pane count is clamped to 1..12.
Growing adds empty (unstarted) panes; it never starts programs on its own.
Shrinking removes unstarted panes first, newest first.
When only started sessions remain, shrinking offers to remove one started session and asks first.
Groups holding several tabs or a non-terminal tab are skipped when choosing what to remove.

Each group keeps its own tab strip and active tab; creating or closing a tab in one group never changes another group's active tab, and closing a group's last tab removes the group and moves focus to a neighbouring group.
acceptance: Going from 4 to 6 panes adds 2 empty panes and leaves the 4 running sessions untouched.
Going from 6 to 4 with 2 unstarted panes removes those 2 without any prompt.
Asking for 13 panes yields 12.

cards.title: Add and remove session shortcuts
cards.user_does: Presses the add-session or remove-session shortcut.
cards.user_sees: One pane is added to or removed from the grid, following the pane-count rules.
rules: Both shortcuts exist but have no default key; the user assigns them.
The on-screen minus/plus stepper was removed on 2026-10-05; only the shortcuts remain.
Remove follows the remove-session default (ask, stop or sleep) for a started session.
acceptance: With keys assigned, add then remove returns the grid to its previous pane count.

cards.title: Confirm before removing a started session
cards.user_does: Removes a pane whose session has already started.
cards.user_sees: A confirmation asks whether to stop the session, put it to sleep, or cancel.
rules: The default reaction is configurable: ask, stop, or sleep.
Cancel has focus when the dialog opens, so Enter does not destroy work.
Unstarted panes are removed without a prompt.
Sessions are classified (unstarted, running agent, idle shell) before deciding whether to ask.
acceptance: Pressing Enter immediately on the dialog leaves the session running.
With the default set to stop, removing a started session stops it without a dialog.

cards.title: Grid layout arrangement for each pane count
cards.user_does: Picks a layout preset or lets the grid arrange itself.
cards.user_sees: Panes are arranged in balanced rows for the chosen count (1, 2, 4, 6, 9, 12) with every pane kept in order.
rules: Every existing pane survives a re-arrangement, in its original order.
Row count is computed from the pane count so panes stay roughly even.
Applying a preset keeps each running session attached to its pane (no restart).
acceptance: Applying the 4-pane preset to 4 running sessions keeps the same 4 sessions with the same output.

cards.title: Default pane count for a new workspace
cards.user_does: Opens a brand-new workspace.
cards.user_sees: The grid starts with the configured number of empty panes (1, 2, 4, 6, 9 or 12).
rules: Seeding happens once per workspace; later setting changes or remounts do not re-seed.
A restored or already-populated workspace is never changed.
The pane already holding the default shell counts toward the total.
Unset or 1 means no extra panes; the classic look never seeds.
acceptance: A new workspace with a default of 4 shows 4 panes, one with a shell and three empty.
Reopening that workspace after adding a pane does not add more panes.

cards.title: Split a pane right or down
cards.user_does: Uses the split shortcut, the header split button, or the pane menu.
cards.user_sees: The pane divides and a new shell opens beside or below it.
rules: Split right: Cmd+D on macOS, Ctrl+Shift+D on Windows/Linux.
Split down: Cmd+Shift+D on macOS, Alt+Shift+D on Windows/Linux.
On Windows/Linux a bare Ctrl+D reaches the shell as end-of-input; split needs Shift.
The new pane starts in the same folder as the pane it was split from.
The header split button splits side by side.
acceptance: Splitting a pane in folder X opens a shell whose working folder is X.
Pressing Ctrl+D in a Linux shell pane sends end-of-input rather than splitting.

cards.title: Starting a session into a full grid makes room
cards.user_does: Launches a new session when no empty pane is free.
cards.user_sees: An existing pane is split to host the new session instead of hiding another one.
rules: An empty pane is used first when one exists.
Otherwise one pane is split; the running sessions keep their output.
acceptance: Launching into a full 4-pane grid ends with 5 visible panes, all four originals still running.

cards.title: Tidy the grid
cards.user_does: Asks the grid to tidy itself after many splits and closes.
cards.user_sees: Pane sizes and positions are rebalanced into an even arrangement.
rules: Tidying never closes or restarts a pane.
acceptance: After uneven splits, tidy gives panes in a row equal widths.

cards.title: Equalize pane sizes
cards.user_does: Chooses Equalize from the pane menu or an assigned shortcut.
cards.user_sees: All split panes in the tab snap to equal sizes.
rules: Shown in the pane menu only when the tab is split.
Has no default key; the menu shows a key hint only once one is assigned.
Equalizing in one tab is broadcast so other views of the same tab follow.
acceptance: Three panes of 50/25/25 become one third each.

cards.title: Resize panes by dragging dividers
cards.user_does: Drags the line between two panes.
cards.user_sees: The panes resize live; the divider is a thin coloured line.
rules: Divider thickness defaults to 3 px.
Divider colour has separate light and dark values (zinc tones by default).
If the pointer is lost mid-drag (left the window, capture lost), the drag still finishes cleanly instead of sticking.
acceptance: Releasing the mouse outside the window ends the drag at the last position.

cards.title: Inactive panes dim
cards.user_does: Clicks into one pane of a split.
cards.user_sees: Other panes fade slightly; the focused pane is fully opaque.
rules: Active pane opacity 1; inactive opacity is a setting.
The fade animates over about 140 ms.
acceptance: Focusing pane B fades pane A within a fraction of a second.

cards.title: Move focus between panes
cards.user_does: Presses next-pane or previous-pane.
cards.user_sees: Keyboard focus moves to the neighbouring pane in order, wrapping around.
rules: Cmd/Ctrl+] for next, Cmd/Ctrl+[ for previous.
acceptance: With 3 panes focused on the last, next goes to the first.

cards.title: Expand one pane to fill, then restore
cards.user_does: Clicks the header expand button, the pane menu item, or Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Enter.
cards.user_sees: The pane fills the space; pressing again restores the previous layout.
rules: In a split tab, the pane fills its tab.
A single-pane session window expands over the whole grid instead.
Only one expanded group per workspace; it is cleared when restored.
Expanding and collapsing does not restart or clear the terminal.
acceptance: Expanding then restoring returns every pane to its prior size.
Scrollback in the expanded pane is unchanged after restore.

cards.title: Close a pane
cards.user_does: Presses Cmd/Ctrl+W in a pane, the header close button, or Close Pane in the menu.
cards.user_sees: That pane closes and its neighbours take the space; closing the last pane closes the tab.
rules: Close applies to the focused pane only, not its siblings.
A pane running a process asks first (see running-process confirmation).
The layout stays consistent after closing (no gaps or ghost panes).
Closing a pane ends its program, forcing it if it does not exit.
acceptance: Closing the middle of three panes leaves two panes filling the area.

cards.title: Drag a pane to rearrange the split
cards.user_does: Grabs a pane header and drops it on another position.
cards.user_sees: The pane moves; its session keeps running.
rules: The drag handle only appears when the tab has more than one pane.
Dropping onto a tab bar or edge can split or move it into another group.
acceptance: Dragging pane A to the right of pane B swaps their order with output intact.

cards.title: Move a pane out into its own tab
cards.user_does: Detaches a split pane into a new tab.
cards.user_sees: The pane becomes its own tab with the same running session.
rules: The source split shrinks back; nothing restarts.
A finished agent's result stays recognised as the same run when its pane is moved out, even after several moves, so it is neither lost nor listed twice.
acceptance: After detaching, the new tab shows the same scrollback.

cards.title: Panes keep their identity across layout changes
cards.user_does: Splits, rearranges, applies presets or restores the app.
cards.user_sees: Each running program stays in its pane; nothing restarts or duplicates.
rules: A split, move or preset never respawns an existing session.
Output from one session never shows up in another pane.
Duplicate replays into the same pane are suppressed.
acceptance: After 10 random splits and moves, each pane still shows its own session.

cards.title: Focus follows mouse
cards.user_does: Turns on focus-follows-mouse.
cards.user_sees: Hovering over a pane focuses it without a click.
rules: Off by default.
acceptance: With the setting on, moving the pointer into pane B lets typing go to B.

cards.title: Every pane shows a header with title and usage
cards.user_does: Looks at any pane.
cards.user_sees: A header row on every pane shows who is running, the session name and the session usage percentage.
rules: Shown on every pane, single or split, since 2026-10-05.
The usage meter shows context use against the session cap.
Never drawn over hidden content.
acceptance: A single-pane grid still shows the header.

cards.title: Pane header identity: agent, name, program, status
cards.user_does: Glances at a pane header.
cards.user_sees: A status dot, the agent mark, the session name, the program name and a status word.
rules: The dot has an accessible label naming its state.
A plain shell shows a generic terminal label and glyph.
The session name falls back to the tab title, or to a generated title when that option is on.
acceptance: A plain shell pane reads as a terminal with a neutral status.
Screen readers announce the dot state.

cards.title: Status word colour reflects what the agent needs
cards.user_does: Watches the pane header while an agent runs.
cards.user_sees: The status word is tinted: working, needs you, done or neutral.
rules: Working or monitoring shows the working tone.
Waiting, permission or blocked shows the needs-you tone and marks the pane as needing the user.
Done shows the done tone; anything else is neutral.
acceptance: A permission prompt flips the word to the needs-you tone within one status update.

cards.title: Branch chip in the pane header
cards.user_does: Works in a git worktree.
cards.user_sees: A small chip with the branch name; detached checkouts show a short commit id.
rules: No chip for a plain folder workspace.
Hovering the chip shows the full branch name.
acceptance: A pane in branch feature/x shows that branch; a non-git folder shows no chip.

cards.title: Finished-while-away glow and age label
cards.user_does: Comes back to a grid where an agent finished while not looking.
cards.user_sees: That pane has a soft green glow and its status reads Done with how long ago.
rules: The age reads just now in the first minute, then minutes ago; it refreshes every minute.
The glow clears once the pane is focused.
The glow is static (no animation) to avoid constant repaints.
Age uses the same finish time as the Board and sidebar.
acceptance: A pane that finished 3 minutes ago, unseen, shows Done with 3m and a glow.
Clicking into it removes the glow.

cards.title: Narrow panes drop header items in a set order
cards.user_does: Shrinks a pane until the header runs out of room.
cards.user_sees: Header items disappear one by one; the dot, agent mark and session name always stay.
rules: First the branch chip goes (around 344 px).
Then the program name (around 264 px).
Then the action buttons (around 204 px).
Then the status word (around 134 px).
The session name truncates rather than disappearing.
acceptance: At 250 px wide the header shows dot, mark, name, status word and buttons but no branch or program name.

cards.title: Pane header buttons
cards.user_does: Uses the buttons at the right of a pane header.
cards.user_sees: More (opens the pane menu), expand, split, close, always in that order.
rules: Close is always shown.
Expand is disabled for a lone pane in the classic look; in the clean look it expands the session window.
The split button stays transparent on hover (no flash).
Right-clicking the header opens the same pane menu.
acceptance: The four buttons appear in the same order on every pane.

cards.title: Pane header density
cards.user_does: Chooses comfortable or compact headers.
cards.user_sees: Compact makes the pane header shorter.
rules: Two values: comfortable (default) and compact.
The Views & sessions settings section is folded by the owner; the knob may move to Terminal & sessions or become fixed.
acceptance: Compact headers are visibly shorter than comfortable.

cards.title: Name a pane
cards.user_does: Chooses Set Title in the pane menu (or an assigned shortcut) and types a name.
cards.user_sees: An inline field in the header; the name replaces the program-derived title.
rules: Enter or Tab saves, Escape cancels, clicking away saves.
An Enter that only confirms an IME candidate does not save.
Clear Pane Title appears only when a custom title is set and returns to the automatic title.
Both actions have no default key; they work once assigned.
The field stays open for typing the first time it opens from the menu.
acceptance: Typing a Korean name with an IME and confirming the candidate keeps the field open.

cards.title: Clean look for the terminal grid
cards.user_does: Uses the clean grid look (default for new installs).
cards.user_sees: Each session is a rounded window with gaps between them; the header carries its own controls.
rules: Rounded corners around 14 px with about 8 px gaps.
A group with a single tab hides its tab strip.
The full (classic) look keeps the older chrome.
New installs land on the clean look; existing profiles keep what they had.
acceptance: A new install shows rounded session windows with gaps.

cards.title: Needs-you strip above the grid
cards.user_does: Has sessions waiting on a permission or a question.
cards.user_sees: A pinned row above the grid lists those sessions in order; clicking one jumps to it.
rules: Lists only this grid's sessions waiting on permission or a question.
Empty and out of the way when nothing waits.
Can be turned off (part of the folded Views & sessions settings).
acceptance: Two waiting sessions appear in the strip in grid order; resolving one removes it.

cards.title: Jump to the next session that needs you
cards.user_does: Presses the needs-you shortcut.
cards.user_sees: Focus jumps to the next pane waiting on the user.
rules: Cmd+Shift+J on macOS, Ctrl+J on Windows/Linux.
Repeated presses cycle through all waiting sessions.
acceptance: With two waiting sessions, two presses visit both.

cards.title: Answer an agent permission prompt from Kolux
cards.user_does: Approves, denies or answers a waiting agent from a Kolux control.
cards.user_sees: The answer is typed into the agent only if the prompt is still showing.
rules: If the prompt has gone or changed, the answer is not sent.
Answers never land in a plain shell by mistake.
acceptance: Approving after the agent already moved on sends nothing.

cards.title: Pane footer and message bar retired
cards.user_does: Used to see a strip under each pane and a message bar for typing to the agent.
cards.user_sees: Both are gone; typing goes straight to the terminal.
rules: Retired on 2026-10-05.
The Swarm footer keeps status plus Approve/Deny/Answer; the Agents view keeps its own composer.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Session stepper (minus/plus) retired
cards.user_does: Used to click minus/plus to change the pane count.
cards.user_sees: The stepper is gone; the add/remove shortcuts remain.
rules: Retired 2026-10-05 with the clean look.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Attention ring on panes
cards.user_does: Would see an attention ring on a pane needing the user.
cards.user_sees: Off by default behind an experimental flag; the unread and done-glow paths are used instead.
rules: When off, background attention falls back to marking the worktree unread.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Pane right-click menu
cards.user_does: Right-clicks inside a pane or presses the header More button.
cards.user_sees: A menu of copy, paste, agent, layout, title, ID and close actions.
rules: Order: Copy, Select All, Paste; agent actions; Split Right, Split Down; Equalize; Expand/Collapse; Set Title, Clear Title; copy IDs; Copy terminal diagnostics; Close Pane; Clear Screen.
Items appear only when they apply (equalize only when split, expand only when expandable, clear title only when set, close only when closable).
Close Pane is styled as destructive.
The menu dismisses on Escape or an outside click.
On Windows with right-click-to-paste on, right-click pastes instead (see that card).
The click that opened the menu does not immediately close it.
acceptance: In an unsplit pane the menu has no Equalize item.

cards.title: Copy session, terminal and pane IDs
cards.user_does: Chooses a copy-ID item in the pane menu.
cards.user_sees: The ID goes to the clipboard, with a success or failure notice.
rules: Copy Session ID appears only when the agent's session identity is known.
Copy Terminal ID and Copy Pane ID are always available.
A failed clipboard write reports failure instead of claiming success.
acceptance: Copy Session ID on a Claude pane puts that session's ID on the clipboard.

cards.title: Fork or continue an agent session
cards.user_does: Chooses Continue in new session, Fork Agent Session, or Copy Context in the pane menu.
cards.user_sees: A new session continues the conversation, or a dialog sets up a fork, or the context is copied.
rules: Shown only for agent panes whose session can be continued.
Fork opens a dialog before anything starts.
Copy Context copies a text summary of the session for pasting elsewhere.
Pressing create twice while it is working starts only one fork.
acceptance: Continue in new session on a Claude pane opens a second pane resuming that conversation.

cards.title: Quick commands menu
cards.user_does: Picks a saved command from a quick-commands menu or pane submenu.
cards.user_sees: The command is typed into the terminal.
rules: Quick commands lived in the tab bar, the pane menu submenu and an unbound shortcut.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: quick-commands menu is in the owner's table 1b cut list. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Switch a pane between chat and terminal view
cards.user_does: Toggles an agent pane into a chat view.
cards.user_sees: Available only when native chat is enabled, which is off by default.
rules: The menu item is hidden unless native chat is on.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: New terminal tab and tab create menu
cards.user_does: Presses Cmd/Ctrl+T or uses the new-tab menu.
cards.user_sees: A new terminal tab, or a chosen browser or markdown tab, opens in the workspace.
rules: New terminal: Cmd/Ctrl+T.
New browser: Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+B; new markdown: Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+M; open markdown: Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+O.
The new tab is focused and ready to type.
A new terminal starts in the workspace folder; a requested start folder may be relative to the workspace or an absolute folder outside it.
If the requested start folder is missing, the terminal starts in the workspace folder; an existing folder outside the workspace is kept.
acceptance: Cmd/Ctrl+T opens a shell in the workspace folder with the cursor ready.
cards.compat: keybinding ids tab.newTerminal, tab.newBrowser, tab.newMarkdown, tab.openMarkdown

cards.title: New agent tab
cards.user_does: Uses the new-agent shortcut or picks an agent from the new-tab menu.
cards.user_sees: A tab opens with the chosen agent already launching.
rules: New default agent: Cmd+Alt+T on macOS.
Each installed agent also gets its own new-tab action, unbound by default.
acceptance: Choosing Claude from the menu opens a tab whose header shows Claude starting.

cards.title: Type a URL or path in the new-tab box
cards.user_does: Types into the new-tab entry box.
cards.user_sees: Matching actions: open a URL in the browser, open a file, search open tabs or history.
rules: http/https, localhost-style dev URLs and private IPv4 addresses are treated as web addresses (bare IPs get http).
Local paths are recognised and open as files; results put the file name before its folder.
Recent entries are remembered and shown by recency.
Arrow keys move through results; Enter runs the highlighted one.
acceptance: Typing 192.168.1.10:3000 offers to open http://192.168.1.10:3000 in the browser.

cards.title: Choose the Windows shell for a new terminal
cards.user_does: Opens the shell menu on Windows.
cards.user_sees: Choices of PowerShell, Command Prompt and Git Bash for the new terminal.
rules: Default shell is PowerShell.
PowerShell Auto uses PowerShell 7 when installed, else Windows PowerShell.
The menu shows only for a local Windows client.
The WSL entries belong to area 18 and are dropped (see WSL card).
A Windows tab keeps the icon of the shell it actually started with.
acceptance: With PowerShell 7 installed and Auto selected, the new tab runs PowerShell 7.

cards.title: Close tabs in bulk
cards.user_does: Uses Close tab, Close all, Close others, Close to the right or Close to the left.
cards.user_sees: Those tabs close, each following the running-process and pinned-tab rules.
rules: Close tab Cmd/Ctrl+W (closes the focused pane when the tab is split); close all Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+W.
Close others and Close to the right are in the tab menu and disabled when nothing would close.
Close to the right uses the visible tab order.
Closing the last terminal keeps the worktree open.
Close to the left is also in the tab menu.
Closing the active tab returns to the tab used before it, otherwise to its right neighbour (left if it was last).
When nothing is left open, the workspace shows its empty start view.
acceptance: Close to the right on the last tab is disabled.

cards.title: Ask before closing a terminal that is still running something
cards.user_does: Closes a tab or pane while a program is running in it.
cards.user_sees: A confirmation explains that the running process will stop; the close happens only after confirming.
rules: Kolux checks for running child processes first; an idle shell closes without asking.
If the check fails, Kolux closes anyway rather than blocking (fails open).
A split tab asks once, not once per pane.
Keyboard and mouse close follow the same policy.
A setting turns the confirmation off.
The confirmation names the tab being closed, so closing a background tab is never ambiguous.
acceptance: Closing a tab running a dev server asks; closing an idle shell does not.

cards.title: Pin tabs; pinned tabs ask before closing
cards.user_does: Pins a tab from its menu, then closes it.
cards.user_sees: Pinned tabs sit first with a pin icon; closing one asks first, while a bulk kill-all closes pinned terminals without a second prompt.
rules: On by default; can be turned off.
Close others and close all skip pinned tabs unless confirmed.
Pin Tab and Unpin Tab are in the tab menu; pinned tabs show a pin icon and sit before unpinned tabs.
Close is disabled in the menu for a pinned tab, and middle-click does not close it.
Close to the right and Close to the left also skip pinned tabs.
acceptance: Cmd/Ctrl+W on a pinned tab shows the confirmation.

cards.title: Reopen a closed tab
cards.user_does: Presses Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+T after closing a tab.
cards.user_sees: The last closed terminal tab comes back in its previous folder.
rules: Up to 10 closed tabs are remembered, newest first.
The folder is remapped when the original path form no longer exists (Windows).
acceptance: Closing three tabs and pressing reopen three times brings all three back in reverse order.

cards.title: Rename a tab
cards.user_does: Double-clicks a tab, uses the tab menu, or presses Cmd+R on macOS.
cards.user_sees: An inline field to rename the tab.
rules: Enter saves, Escape cancels; an IME candidate Enter does not save.
Pasting while renaming goes into the field, not the terminal.
acceptance: Pasting text while renaming changes only the tab name.

cards.title: Tab right-click menu
cards.user_does: Right-clicks a tab.
cards.user_sees: Pin or unpin, Change Title, Tab Color, split, close, close others, close to the right and close to the left.
rules: Directional close items are disabled when there is nothing to close.
Split actions move the tab into a split view.
Middle-click closes an unpinned tab.
acceptance: The first tab has close-to-the-left (if present) disabled.

cards.title: Switch to the recent tab with Ctrl+Tab
cards.user_does: Holds Ctrl and presses Tab.
cards.user_sees: A switcher of recent tabs; releasing Ctrl opens the highlighted one.
rules: Default order is most-recently-used; a setting switches it to left-to-right.
acceptance: Ctrl+Tab once from tab C returns to the previously used tab.

cards.title: Cycle tabs by type
cards.user_does: Uses the next/previous tab shortcuts.
cards.user_sees: Focus moves to the next tab of the same type, any type, or the next terminal.
rules: Same type: Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+] and [.
All types: Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+] and [.
Terminals only: Ctrl+PageDown and Ctrl+PageUp.
Tab cycling and go-to-number follow the strip's visible order, including after drag reordering; tabs whose content is gone are skipped.
acceptance: From a terminal, next-same-type skips browser tabs.
cards.compat: keybinding ids tab.nextSameType, tab.previousSameType, tab.nextAllTypes, tab.previousAllTypes, tab.nextTerminal, tab.previousTerminal

cards.title: Go to a tab by number
cards.user_does: Presses Ctrl+1..9 on macOS or Alt+1..9 on Windows/Linux.
cards.user_sees: The tab at that position is selected.
rules: A number beyond the tab count does nothing.
acceptance: With 3 tabs, the 2 shortcut selects the middle tab.

cards.title: Search open tabs
cards.user_does: Searches open tabs by name from the tab entry box.
cards.user_sees: Matching open tabs appear and can be jumped to.
rules: Stale results are dropped as the query changes.
Matches tab names only; a query matching just the worktree name finds nothing.
acceptance: Typing part of a tab name lists that tab.

cards.title: Reorder tabs by dragging
cards.user_does: Drags a tab along the tab strip.
cards.user_sees: The tab moves to the drop point.
rules: Dropping on the right half of a tab places it after; left half before.
Dropping a tab on itself changes nothing.

Dragging a tab onto the outer edge band of a group opens a new group on that side; dropping in the centre or on a tab strip adds it to that group; hovering a strip never counts as a top-edge split; a drop that would recreate the current layout does nothing.
acceptance: Dragging tab 1 onto the right half of tab 3 makes it third.

cards.title: Tab activity indicators
cards.user_does: Watches the tab strip while agents run.
cards.user_sees: Each terminal tab shows a spinner while working and badges for permission, unread or done.
rules: Badge priority: working, then permission, then unread, then done.
A bell or a finished agent in a tab not being viewed marks it unread.
The spinner sits beside the agent's icon.
Stale self-written question titles are not treated as a live question.
Done shows a green check, waiting for permission shows a question mark, an unvisited completion keeps a bell, and an idle shell shows only its identity icon.
acceptance: A background tab whose agent finishes shows an unread badge until viewed.

cards.title: Tab title tooltip and generated titles
cards.user_does: Hovers a tab, or turns on generated tab titles.
cards.user_sees: A tooltip with the full title; with the option on, tabs get short generated names.
rules: Generated titles are off by default.
acceptance: Hovering a truncated tab shows its full title.

cards.title: Tab strip overflow scrollbar
cards.user_does: Opens more tabs than fit.
cards.user_sees: A thin scroll bar under the tabs that thickens on hover and can be dragged or clicked.
rules: Hidden when nothing overflows.
Idle height 2 px, 3 px on hover.
Mouse wheel over it scrolls the tab strip.
acceptance: With 30 tabs, dragging the thumb scrolls the tabs.

cards.title: Tab titles follow the running program
cards.user_does: Runs a program or agent that sets its window title.
cards.user_sees: The tab and pane titles update to match; the agent is recognised from the title.
rules: Agent identity found in titles is used for the status dot and icon.
Hook-reported status takes precedence over title guesses when both exist.

An agent started by hand in a plain shell is recognised from the running program when a command starts and forgotten when the shell prompt returns; the shell end-of-command marker is seen even when it arrives split across output chunks, and replayed or restored output never counts as a command starting or finishing.
In a split tab the agent icon comes only from the focused pane; when that pane runs a plain shell, no agent from a sibling pane is shown.
A live agent's own report of what it is outranks a saved record from a sleeping session.
acceptance: Starting Claude in a shell tab changes the tab title and icon to Claude.

cards.title: Floating workspace panel
cards.user_does: Presses Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+A or the floating button.
cards.user_sees: A floating panel over the app with its own terminal, agent, browser and markdown tabs.
rules: The trigger button sits at the bottom right by default; it can be moved and its place is remembered.
The button position is kept inside the window when the window shrinks.
The floating-workspace settings section is cut; the feature stays with fixed defaults.
Opening the panel puts typing focus in its active terminal straight away.
acceptance: Pressing Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+A twice opens then closes the panel.

cards.title: Move, resize and maximize the floating panel
cards.user_does: Drags the panel title bar or edges, or maximizes it.
cards.user_sees: The panel moves and resizes; its size and place are remembered.
rules: Saved size and place are restored next time; broken saved data falls back to defaults.
The panel is kept inside the window; it can touch but not cover the macOS title bar.
Maximize keeps the normal size for when it is restored.
Maximize: Cmd+Alt+Shift+A on macOS; minimize has no default key.
Dragging from a tab icon does not move the panel.
acceptance: Resizing the panel, closing and reopening it shows the same size.

cards.title: Floating panel tabs and close behaviour
cards.user_does: Opens and closes tabs inside the floating panel.
cards.user_sees: Tabs can be added, reordered and closed; the panel stays open after closing a tab.
rules: An empty panel shows an empty state with actions and can be minimized from there; Cmd/Ctrl+W on it minimizes.
Opening an empty panel does not auto-create a terminal.
A new agent tab started from the panel is selected and focused.
A program exiting is kept separate from the user closing the pane.
Unsaved markdown tabs ask before closing, one at a time.
Floating terminals start in the home folder by default; trusted folders are remembered.
acceptance: Closing the last tab leaves the panel open on its empty state.

cards.title: Shortcuts inside the floating panel
cards.user_does: Uses tab shortcuts while focus is in the floating panel.
cards.user_sees: New tab, open markdown, tab switching, rename and tab-by-number act on the floating panel, not the main window.
rules: Shortcuts past the visible tab count are swallowed without action.
Double-tap shortcuts reset when the window loses focus.
Key chords the panel has no action for pass through untouched.
acceptance: Cmd/Ctrl+T in the floating panel opens a floating tab.

cards.title: Floating button shows pending activity
cards.user_does: Closes the floating panel while something in it is still active.
cards.user_sees: A small dot on the floating button signals pending activity.
rules: The dot hides while the panel is open or when nothing is pending.
acceptance: An agent finishing in the closed panel shows the dot.

cards.title: Mobile emulator tab in the floating workspace
cards.user_does: Opens an iOS/Android emulator tab.
cards.user_sees: A simulator tab alongside terminals.
rules: Part of the mobile emulator pane, area 18.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: remote hosts, web runtime, WSL execution and mobile are area 18, dropped by the owner. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Copy terminal selection, never silently
cards.user_does: Selects text and presses the copy shortcut or menu item.
cards.user_sees: The text is on the clipboard; if the copy fails a notice says so.
rules: Copy: Cmd+C on macOS; Ctrl+Shift+C on Windows/Linux, and Ctrl+C when text is selected.
On failure the selection is kept and one notice shows (repeated failures are throttled).
An empty selection never reports success.
Focus returns to the pane after copying.
On macOS the copy shortcut follows the letter the keyboard layout produces, not the physical key position.
acceptance: With the clipboard locked by another app, copying shows a failure notice and the selection remains.

cards.title: Copy on select
cards.user_does: Turns on copy on select.
cards.user_sees: Selecting text copies it automatically.
rules: Off by default.
Failure notices are throttled so dragging does not spam them.
acceptance: With the option on, dragging over text puts it on the clipboard.

cards.title: Select all in a terminal
cards.user_does: Presses select-all.
cards.user_sees: All terminal text is selected.
rules: Cmd+A on macOS; Ctrl+Shift+A on Windows/Linux, leaving bare Ctrl+A to the shell.
acceptance: Ctrl+A in a Linux shell moves to the line start rather than selecting.

cards.title: Paste into a terminal
cards.user_does: Presses paste or uses Edit, Paste.
cards.user_sees: Clipboard text is typed into the focused pane only.
rules: Cmd+V on macOS; Ctrl+V, Ctrl+Shift+V and Shift+Insert on Windows/Linux.
The Edit menu paste goes to whichever window and pane has focus.
Paste never lands in a different pane than the one focused (including splits and rename fields).
If the target pane changes while the clipboard is still being read, the paste is cancelled rather than sent elsewhere.
A paste made while an agent's starting prompt is still being typed waits for it, so the two never interleave.
A brief loss of focus during the clipboard read, with focus returning to the same pane, does not cancel the paste.
acceptance: Pasting with a split focused on pane B never types into pane A.

cards.title: Safe multi-line paste
cards.user_does: Pastes several lines into a shell or agent.
cards.user_sees: The lines arrive as one paste and do not run line by line.
rules: Bracketed paste is used when the program supports it.
On Windows, multi-line text is forced onto the bracketed path.
Single-line text takes the ordinary fast path.
Clipboard content is never written to logs.
acceptance: Pasting three commands into PowerShell does not execute them one by one.

cards.title: Paste a screenshot as a file path
cards.user_does: Pastes when the clipboard holds an image.
cards.user_sees: The image is saved to a file and its path is pasted for the agent to read.
rules: The path is bracket-pasted even when the program has not asked for bracketed paste.
The image is still tried when reading clipboard text fails.
Text clipboards skip the image check entirely.
Failures to extract or paste the image are reported, not swallowed.
Pasting several images at once and Linux paths for WSL are not shipped (TERM-9, TERM-8).
acceptance: Pasting a screenshot into a Claude pane inserts a path to a saved image.

cards.title: Large pastes stay responsive
cards.user_does: Pastes a very large block of text.
cards.user_sees: The app stays responsive while the text is fed to the terminal in chunks.
rules: Large pastes are chunked and yield between chunks.
Clipboard text over the size limit is rejected with a message.
acceptance: Pasting several megabytes leaves the rest of the app clickable during the paste.

cards.title: Right-click to paste
cards.user_does: Right-clicks in a pane.
cards.user_sees: On Windows it pastes; on macOS and Linux it opens the pane menu.
rules: Default follows the platform; the user can change it.
acceptance: On Windows, right-click with text on the clipboard pastes it.

cards.title: Middle-click paste of the selection
cards.user_does: Middle-clicks in a pane.
cards.user_sees: The last selected text is pasted (Linux primary selection style).
rules: On by default on Linux; off elsewhere unless turned on.
acceptance: On Linux, selecting text then middle-clicking pastes it.

cards.title: Drop files onto a terminal
cards.user_does: Drags files from the OS or the file tree onto a pane or its header.
cards.user_sees: Their paths are typed in, quoted for the shell.
rules: Paths go to the pane under the drop, not the focused one.
Image files are recognised by extension.
If the target terminal changed before the write, nothing is pasted.
Timeouts and rejected writes show an error without exposing the dropped paths.
Windows paths are quoted for Windows shells; WSL and SSH conversions belong to area 18.
acceptance: Dropping a file with spaces in its name pastes a correctly quoted path.

cards.title: Programs can copy to the clipboard (OSC 52)
cards.user_does: Copies inside tmux, Zellij, Neovim or similar.
cards.user_sees: The text reaches the system clipboard.
rules: On by default; programs can never read the clipboard back.
If blocked, a notice once per session links to the setting.
If the write cannot be confirmed, a notice once per session says so.
Profiles migrated to default-on see a one-time notice.
Payload size is capped.
acceptance: Yanking in Neovim inside tmux makes the text pasteable in another app.

cards.title: Clear the screen
cards.user_does: Presses Cmd/Ctrl+K or picks Clear Screen in the pane menu.
cards.user_sees: The visible terminal and its scrollback are cleared.
rules: Saved link ranges from before the clear are dropped.
acceptance: After clearing, scrolling up shows no old output.

cards.title: Find text in a terminal
cards.user_does: Presses Cmd/Ctrl+F in a pane.
cards.user_sees: A find bar highlights matches in the output and scrollback.
rules: Invalid search patterns do not crash the find bar.
Very long search text is capped.
acceptance: Searching a word present 3 times lets the user step through all 3.

cards.title: Zoom the terminal font
cards.user_does: Uses zoom in, zoom out or reset (shortcut or View menu).
cards.user_sees: The terminal text gets bigger or smaller.
rules: Only the pane that owns keyboard focus reacts.
View menu holds Zoom In, Zoom Out and Reset Size; from the menu they change the focused terminal's text size.
acceptance: Zooming in twice then reset returns to the configured font size.

cards.title: Kolux shortcuts versus shell keys
cards.user_does: Presses key combos inside a terminal.
cards.user_sees: Kolux keeps its own shortcuts while the shell keeps its editing keys.
rules: Policy defaults to Kolux-first.
macOS readline Ctrl chords go to the shell.
On macOS, Cmd+Left/Right jump to line start/end; Cmd+Up/Down jump to the top/bottom of scrollback.
Alt/Option+Arrow moves by word on every platform.
Custom pane keybindings are honoured.
On Windows, Ctrl+Arrow moves by word in the shell.
acceptance: Ctrl+R in a shell opens reverse history search, not a Kolux action.

cards.title: Shift+Enter makes a new line in agents
cards.user_does: Presses Shift+Enter in an agent prompt.
cards.user_sees: A new line is inserted instead of sending.
rules: Uses the encoding the agent understands (enhanced keyboard mode or a Windows-compatible form).
Ctrl+Enter goes only to programs known to accept it.
Plain shells keep normal Enter behaviour.
Shift+Enter handling stays with the agent's pane after that pane is split.
acceptance: Shift+Enter in Codex on Windows adds a line without submitting.

cards.title: Option key as Alt on macOS
cards.user_does: Uses Option combos in a macOS terminal.
cards.user_sees: Option either types special characters or acts as Alt for the shell.
rules: Auto checks the keyboard layout so non-US users can still type @, € and brackets.
Left-only or right-only Option-as-Alt are available.
Option+B/F/D map to word movement and delete.
Fresh installs default to Auto.
acceptance: On a German layout in Auto, Option+L types @.

cards.title: Enhanced keyboard protocol for modern TUIs
cards.user_does: Uses a program that asks for the enhanced (kitty) keyboard protocol.
cards.user_sees: Modifier combos reach the program exactly.
rules: Only used while the program has asked for it.
Dead keys still start accented characters.
Cmd or Ctrl combos are not intercepted.
acceptance: Option+digit in a kitty-mode program arrives as an encoded key, not a symbol.

cards.title: Typing in Korean, Chinese and Japanese
cards.user_does: Types with an input method (IME).
cards.user_sees: The composing text shows in place; Enter commits the composition without also running the command.
rules: Korean syllables are flushed correctly before digits and on Enter.
Chinese pinyin and Japanese composition are supported on macOS, Windows and Linux.
Cancelled compositions disappear cleanly.
Bytes sent to the program match what was typed exactly.
The input method's candidate window stays anchored at the cursor while composing.
Sogou-style Chinese input and Vietnamese letter-replacing input methods work.
Modifier chords such as the IME on/off toggle are not mistaken for composition keys.
On Windows, macOS and Linux a native Korean input method works, including at the end of a row.
acceptance: Typing a Korean word then Enter submits the word once.

cards.title: Yen key types backslash (JIS keyboards)
cards.user_does: Turns on yen-to-backslash on a Japanese keyboard.
cards.user_sees: The yen key types a backslash.
rules: Off by default.
acceptance: With the option on, the yen key types a backslash in the shell.

cards.title: Switch input source shortcut
cards.user_does: Assigns and presses the switch-input-source shortcut.
cards.user_sees: The OS input source switches without the key reaching the terminal.
rules: Unbound by default; only works through an explicit assignment.
acceptance: An ordinary chord is not treated as input-source switching.

cards.title: Control keys work on non-Latin keyboard layouts
cards.user_does: Presses Ctrl+C or similar with a Cyrillic or other non-Latin layout active.
cards.user_sees: The control key acts as if on a Latin layout.
rules: Mapping uses the physical key.
macOS system-wide key remaps are honoured.
acceptance: Ctrl+C on a Russian layout interrupts the running program.

cards.title: Hide the mouse pointer while typing
cards.user_does: Turns on hide-while-typing and types.
cards.user_sees: The pointer disappears until the mouse moves.
rules: Off by default.
acceptance: Typing hides the pointer; moving the mouse shows it.

cards.title: Selecting text in mouse-capturing programs
cards.user_does: Tries to select text in a program that captures the mouse.
cards.user_sees: A hint explains holding Shift to select.
rules: A program that died leaving mouse capture on does not keep capturing after reattach.
acceptance: Shift-drag in a mouse-capturing TUI selects text.

cards.title: Mouse wheel scroll speed
cards.user_does: Scrolls with the wheel or trackpad.
cards.user_sees: Normal, fast (with modifier) and full-screen-app scrolling at tuned speeds.
rules: Normal 1.15, fast 5, inside full-screen apps 1.
Queued wheel events in a TUI drain instead of piling up.
Each notched wheel tick reaches a mouse-capturing program at once, and a scroll setting for full-screen programs scales those reports.
acceptance: Holding the fast modifier scrolls several times further per notch.

cards.title: Scroll position: follow output or stay put
cards.user_does: Scrolls up to read while output keeps coming.
cards.user_sees: The view stays where the user put it; at the bottom it follows new output.
rules: Scrolling back to the bottom resumes following.
Switching tabs and back keeps the same scroll position.
Pending focus changes never flip a pinned view into following.
acceptance: Reading 200 lines up while a build prints keeps that spot until the user scrolls down.

cards.title: Scrollback length
cards.user_does: Scrolls back through long output.
cards.user_sees: Earlier output is kept up to the scrollback limit.
rules: A default row limit applies; long tables restore their scroll position after a tab switch.
acceptance: Output beyond the limit is trimmed from the oldest end.

cards.title: Clickable web links in output
cards.user_does: Holds the modifier and clicks a URL in terminal output.
cards.user_sees: The link opens in the system browser or the Kolux browser.
rules: Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere; a hover hint names where it will open.
URLs wrapped across lines (soft or hard wrap) are joined.
Programs' own hyperlinks (OSC 8) are clickable, including after restore.
Open-in-Kolux is off by default; the modifier can invert the destination.
Clicks meant as links are not forwarded to mouse-capturing programs.
Shift plus the link modifier always opens the system browser.
The link highlight and hover hint clear when the window loses focus.
Non-Latin letters (for example Chinese or Japanese) that belong to a URL path stay part of the link.
acceptance: A URL wrapped over two lines opens as one complete address.

cards.title: Clickable file paths in output
cards.user_does: Clicks a file path or path:line in output.
cards.user_sees: The file opens in the editor at that line.
rules: Relative paths resolve against the pane's folder or the worktree root.
file:// links and program hyperlinks to files are supported.
Network-share paths are not probed on hover.
Trailing punctuation after a bare file name is not part of the link.
acceptance: Clicking src/app.ts:42 opens that file at line 42.

cards.title: Link action menu
cards.user_does: Uses the link menu gesture on a link.
cards.user_sees: A small menu offers to open or copy the link.
rules: On by default; can be turned off, which also removes it from the hover hint.
acceptance: With the menu off, the hover hint no longer mentions it.

cards.title: Link detection never freezes on huge lines
cards.user_does: Prints extremely long lines.
cards.user_sees: The terminal stays responsive.
rules: Link scanning is capped for pathological lines.
acceptance: A 1 MB single line does not freeze the pane.

cards.title: Links to other terminals and orchestration tasks
cards.user_does: Clicks a terminal handle or task reference printed by the coordinator.
cards.user_sees: Kolux focuses that terminal or opens that task.
rules: Only recognised handle formats become links.
acceptance: Clicking a printed terminal handle focuses its pane.

cards.title: Terminal font settings
cards.user_does: Changes the terminal font, size, weight or line height.
cards.user_sees: Text re-renders with the new font.
rules: Defaults: size 14, line height 1, normal and bold weights.
The editor follows the terminal font unless set separately.
The saved font paints at startup with no flash.
acceptance: Changing size to 16 enlarges every pane.

cards.title: Terminal colour themes
cards.user_does: Picks a terminal theme for dark and light mode or matches the app theme.
cards.user_sees: Terminal colours change; light mode can use a separate theme.
rules: Defaults: a Kolux dark theme and a Tango-style light theme, separate light theme on.
Match app theme makes the terminal follow the app colour theme.
Custom themes can be added.
Programs asking the terminal for its colours get correct answers, with no leaked replies at startup.
No flash of the wrong theme at startup.
Programs that subscribe to light/dark changes are told when the mode flips.
acceptance: Switching the app to light mode switches terminals to the light theme.

cards.title: Import settings from Ghostty
cards.user_does: Imports an existing Ghostty config.
cards.user_sees: Matching Kolux terminal settings and themes are filled in; unsupported keys are listed.
rules: Maps font, cursor, colours and palette, padding, split divider colour, unfocused split opacity, scrollback, Option-as-Alt, bold colour, selection characters and hide-mouse-while-typing.
Theme references are resolved from Ghostty's theme folders.
Keys with no Kolux equivalent are reported, not silently dropped.
Focus-follows-mouse is imported; an invalid value is reported, not guessed.
An oversized config file is skipped and reported while settings already imported are kept.
Middle-click paste behaviour (paste the selection) is imported too.
A background blur setting maps to the app's window blur setting; zero means off and is not reported as dropped.
acceptance: Importing a config with an unknown key shows it in the unsupported list.
cards.compat: file format: Ghostty config (key = value) and Ghostty theme files

cards.title: Import Warp themes
cards.user_does: Imports a theme from Warp.
cards.user_sees: A preview of the found Warp themes, then the chosen one is added as a custom theme.
rules: Looks in Warp's theme folders.
Parsing is time-limited so a bad file cannot hang the app.
Theme files that are skipped are listed with a reason, and the reason never shows full folder paths.
Background images and gradients in a Warp theme are left out and reported as skipped.
acceptance: A malformed theme file fails with a message instead of hanging.

cards.title: Cursor style
cards.user_does: Chooses block, bar or underline, blink on or off.
cards.user_sees: The cursor takes that shape.
rules: Default block, blinking.
A program that sets its own cursor shape wins until it hands control back.
An unfocused pane shows a hollow cursor only for block style.
acceptance: Choosing bar persists across restart.

cards.title: Minimum contrast and ligatures
cards.user_does: Uses a theme with weak contrast or a ligature font.
cards.user_sees: Low-contrast text is lifted to stay readable; ligatures show for known ligature fonts.
rules: Ligatures auto: on only for fonts known to have them.
acceptance: Selecting a ligature font shows joined arrows; a plain font does not.

cards.title: GPU rendering with safe fallback
cards.user_does: Runs many terminals.
cards.user_sees: Fast rendering; if the GPU path fails, terminals keep working on the slower path.
rules: Auto uses GPU rendering when supported, otherwise plain rendering; on/off can be forced.
At most 6 GPU contexts at once, hidden tabs included; extra panes use the plain path.
One GPU failure no longer slows every new terminal.
Glyph caches reset after paste bursts and system resume to clear garbled text.
A program's synchronized frame is shown whole, including when a hidden pane is revealed.
acceptance: Opening 10 terminals never shows blank panes.

cards.title: Correct rendering of complex scripts and emoji
cards.user_does: Prints Arabic, CJK, Hangul or emoji tables.
cards.user_sees: Text lines up correctly and the cursor sits in the right cell.
rules: Wide characters take two cells; the cursor matches.
Arabic shaping is shown correctly.
Tables with emoji and wide characters keep a clean right edge after restore and after scrolling.
acceptance: An emoji table renders with aligned columns.

cards.title: Terminals survive quitting and reopening Kolux
cards.user_does: Quits Kolux and opens it again.
cards.user_sees: Every tab, split and session is back with its scrollback; running programs kept running.
rules: A background host keeps sessions alive while the app is closed.
Scrollback survives a clean quit and relaunch.
Restored panes accept input straight away.
The focused pane and an expanded pane come back as they were.
Terminals created from the command line or by automation are restored too.
acceptance: Quit with a build running; reopen; the build output continues in the same pane.

cards.title: Restore after the background host or computer died
cards.user_does: Reopens Kolux after a crash, a killed host or a reboot.
cards.user_sees: Each pane shows its saved output and a fresh shell in the same folder.
rules: Saved history is written safely so a crash leaves a usable copy.
Large histories restore in pieces within memory limits.
A corrupt tab record does not hide the other tabs.
Reopening a worktree does not create duplicate tabs.
Sessions closed on purpose are not brought back.
Older saved histories from very wide terminals still restore.
A local agent that had already finished is not started again on restore.

A pane whose agent was still working resumes the same agent conversation with the settings it was started with, even if settings changed since; if that is not possible it falls back to a fresh shell and shows the restored banner.
Saved output for worktrees that no longer exist is pruned in the background; anything whose owner is uncertain is kept, and nothing is pruned when the list of live worktrees is empty.
After a dead background host is replaced, the rest of a half-typed line is discarded rather than run; the hold ends after a short idle gap or a fixed cap, so typing never stays blocked.
acceptance: After killing the host, reopened panes show their earlier output above a new prompt.

cards.title: Restored-session banner
cards.user_does: Opens a pane that was restored from saved history.
cards.user_sees: A banner marks where restored output ends and live output begins.
rules: Shown only for restored sessions.
Disappears on the first key press or click in the pane.
When the agent conversation could not be resumed and a fresh shell was opened instead, the pane is marked as restored without resume; otherwise it keeps its identity.
acceptance: Typing in a restored pane removes the banner.

cards.title: Background host updates without losing sessions
cards.user_does: Updates Kolux or restarts the terminal host.
cards.user_sees: Live sessions keep running; an outdated host is replaced when safe.
rules: A restart follows a fixed sequence that keeps live sessions.
An idle host with no sessions shuts itself down.
An old-version host is retired after its sessions end.
A slow health check is not treated as dead.

On macOS, a host started by an app copy that no longer exists (after an update or a move) is replaced under the current app before the next new terminal, but only when it holds no live sessions; a host with live sessions is kept running.
acceptance: Updating with 3 running sessions keeps all 3.

cards.title: Host crash containment
cards.user_does: Hits a case where the terminal host keeps crashing.
cards.user_sees: Kolux stops restarting it in a loop and stays usable in a degraded mode.
rules: Repeated deaths in a short window stop respawning.
A preserved host is marked degraded rather than discarded.
Terminals being opened while the host connection drops are retried and still open.
acceptance: A host crashing 5 times quickly is not respawned a 6th time immediately.

cards.title: Terminal error messages in plain words
cards.user_does: Hits a terminal error.
cards.user_sees: A notice explains what happened in plain language, with a restart-host button when that would help.
rules: Internal codes are replaced with readable explanations.
Restart host is offered for stale-host install or folder failures.
Errors Kolux can explain hide the report-issue link; unexplained ones keep it.
The notice never claims a remote shell is dead or alive when it cannot know.
Local errors include a short environment footer.
acceptance: A dead host error shows a readable message without an issue link.

cards.title: Shell exit overlay with restart
cards.user_does: Sees a shell exit or fail to start.
cards.user_sees: An overlay with the exit code and a restart option.
rules: A Git Bash process-limit failure is explained with recovery actions.
Restart retries the original start command, or opens a shell if there was none.
After an agent exits, the pane is left with a clean, working shell.

A normal exit (for example typing exit) closes that pane and its neighbours take the space; when the last pane exits the tab closes, also for tabs parked in the background. The overlay is only for a program that died or failed to start.
A tab closed because its program exited by itself keeps its saved agent session, so it can still be resumed.
acceptance: After a shell crashes, restart gives a working prompt in the same pane.

cards.title: Hidden terminals use less memory
cards.user_does: Leaves many tabs and worktrees open in the background.
cards.user_sees: Background terminals keep running and come back instantly, while memory stays bounded.
rules: Hidden views are parked after a short delay.
Hidden worktrees fall under a retention budget.
The tab the user left on stays mounted.
Bells and exits in parked terminals are still noticed.
Switching back restores the exact screen.
An agent finishing its task is still noticed while its terminal is parked.
A pane whose program exited while parked drops out of the saved layout cleanly.
Hidden or restoring panes still answer a program's colour, cursor-position and device queries promptly, even when the saved backlog overflows.
acceptance: Switching back to a parked tab shows the same screen as before.

cards.title: Fast startup with many saved terminals
cards.user_does: Opens Kolux with many saved tabs.
cards.user_sees: The visible workspace comes up first; hidden tabs start when needed.
rules: Background worktrees mount only the tabs that are needed.
Startup waits for saved state, unless running degraded.
acceptance: With 20 saved tabs, the visible tab is usable before the hidden ones are ready.

cards.title: Recover after sleep, wake and window focus
cards.user_does: Wakes the computer or returns to the window.
cards.user_sees: Terminals redraw correctly at the right size and accept input.
rules: Glyph caches clear on system resume but not on simple focus.
Pane sizes are re-sent after the window settles.
Display scaling changes are repaired.
Slept terminals show their output and accept fresh input after wake.
When the window regains focus, typing returns to the pane that had it, unless the user clicked somewhere else meanwhile.
acceptance: After sleep, a pane shows readable text and responds to typing.

cards.title: Typing and output never get stuck
cards.user_does: Types and watches heavy output.
cards.user_sees: Input stays responsive and output keeps flowing.
rules: A stalled write pipeline recovers on its own.
Lost output deliveries are repaired from the saved buffer.
Keystrokes to a terminal not yet ready are held rather than lost.
Typing latency with agents like Codex stays low.
Output from many busy terminals is paced so the app stays responsive.
Keystrokes held for a terminal that is not yet connected are capped in size.
When a stuck pipeline is recovered the user is told, even if part of the clean-up fails.
acceptance: A pane whose writes wedge resumes rendering and input without reload.

cards.title: Copy terminal diagnostics
cards.user_does: Chooses Copy terminal diagnostics in the pane menu.
cards.user_sees: A diagnostics snapshot is copied for bug reports.
rules: Secrets and personal paths are redacted.
Named in the 0.12.0 release.
If the snapshot cannot be built or copied, a notice says so; it never fails silently.
acceptance: The copied text has no access tokens.

cards.title: Freeze report and render diagnostics
cards.user_does: Would open a freeze report in developer tools.
cards.user_sees: Developer-facing traces of renderer and GPU events.
rules: Kept as internal breadcrumbs; the user-facing path is Copy terminal diagnostics.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Bell and finish notifications
cards.user_does: Has an agent finish or ring the bell while looking elsewhere.
cards.user_sees: A notification, plus unread marks on the tab, pane and worktree.
rules: No unread mark for the pane being looked at.
Hidden tabs and hidden split panes are marked unread.
With Kolux in the background, the selected worktree is marked unread.
Late or stale finish events are dropped.
Notification settings gate what is sent.
acceptance: An agent finishing in a hidden tab sends one notification and marks the tab unread.

cards.title: Shell history per worktree
cards.user_does: Uses the up arrow in a shell.
cards.user_sees: History shows commands from this worktree only.
rules: On by default.
Scopes bash, zsh and fish history per worktree; cmd.exe and unknown shells are left alone.
A history file the user already set is respected.
History folders are private to the user.
History for a deleted worktree is removed, and leftover fish histories are swept.
acceptance: A command run in worktree A does not appear in worktree B's history.

cards.title: Windows terminals behave natively
cards.user_does: Uses terminals on Windows.
cards.user_sees: Commands on PATH resolve, Unicode prints correctly and Git Bash works.

cards.title: Full-screen programs keep their own screen
cards.user_does: Runs a full-screen program such as vim, less or an agent's full-screen view in a pane, then quits it, switches away, or restarts Kolux while it runs.
cards.user_sees: The program owns the pane while it runs; once it quits, the shell output from before it is back exactly as it was and can be scrolled.
rules: Leaving a full-screen program restores the shell screen and its scrollback unchanged.
Scroll positions are kept per screen and never carried from the shell screen to the full-screen one or back.
On reattach or tab return the program's screen comes back and redraws once; a repeat resize repaint at the same size never duplicates content.
Agent views that draw inline on the normal screen and ones that take over the whole screen are both restored cleanly.
A cold restore keeps the output from before an unclosed full-screen session and cuts at the outermost unclosed one.
If a full-screen program dies without handing the screen back, the shell prompt is reset to a usable state.
While a full-screen or mouse-driven program owns the pane, the shell is not treated as ready or idle.
acceptance: Run vim, quit it: earlier shell output is visible and scrollable from where it was.
With an agent in full-screen view, quit Kolux and reopen: the pane shows one clean frame, no doubled content.
Kill the background host while vim is open, reopen: shell output from before vim plus a fresh prompt.

cards.title: Colour-code a tab
cards.user_does: Right-clicks a tab and picks a colour under Tab Color.
cards.user_sees: A small coloured dot shows on that tab; picking None removes it.
rules: Ten choices: none, blue, purple, pink, red, orange, yellow, green, teal and grey.
The colour belongs to that tab only and does not change the terminal's own colours.
acceptance: Right-click a tab, Tab Color then Green: a green dot appears on that tab only.
Tab Color then None: the dot is gone.

cards.title: Programs always see the pane's true size
cards.user_does: Opens, splits, resizes or reveals a pane, or resizes the window, while a program or agent runs in it.
cards.user_sees: Full-screen programs and agents draw at the pane's real width and height; their output never comes out garbled, squeezed or one character per line.
rules: The width and height the running program sees always end up equal to the visible pane's columns and rows, including on first mount, when a tab mounts with a split layout already present, after a split is reparented, and when the window is resized during startup.
A pane resized while hidden catches up when it is shown again; hidden panes that cannot be measured are never resized to a tiny size.
While a divider is being dragged only the final size is sent to the program; a cancelled drag sends no stale size.

Kolux checks the size the terminal actually applied, not only the size it asked for, and re-sends when the two differ; if that check fails it falls back to the requested size and sends once instead of looping.
When the size changes several times in quick succession the program settles on the latest size, never an older one.
acceptance: Start a full-screen program in a split pane and resize the window during startup: the program's column count equals the pane's columns.
Hide a tab, resize the window twice, show the tab again: the program reports the pane's current columns within about a second.
Drag a divider back and forth and release: the program receives the final size and no earlier size after release.
evidence: dumps/tests/03-terminals-panes.txt: 48 size-sync titles (pty-size-reassertion, pty-applied-size-reporting, pty-size-reconcile, pane-pty-resize-hold, column-desync and reveal-stale e2e)

cards.title: First web link click asks where links open
cards.user_does: Holds the link modifier and clicks a web address in terminal output for the first time.
cards.user_sees: Before the link opens, a dialog shows the site it points to and asks whether terminal links should open in the Kolux browser or the system browser; the link then opens where the user chose.
rules: Asked once: the answer becomes the saved link destination and the dialog never comes back, including after a restart.
If links are already set to open in the Kolux browser, the dialog offers keeping that or switching to the system browser instead.
The Kolux browser choice has the keyboard focus; closing the dialog without picking (Escape or a click outside) counts as the system browser and still counts as answered.
Changing the link destination switch by hand also counts as answered, so the dialog never appears after that.
Clicks that already name a destination (Shift plus the link modifier, or a pick from the link action menu) open at once without the dialog.
Several link clicks made while the dialog is up share one question; each waiting link opens with that one answer.
Guided tours hold off while the dialog is showing.
The dialog reminds the user that Shift plus the link modifier opens the system browser for a single click, and says where the choice can be changed later.

The old dialog pointed to a browser settings section that the rebuild cuts; the rebuild puts the link destination switch on the Terminal & sessions page beside the other link options, and the dialog points there.
acceptance: Fresh profile: modifier-click a web address, pick the system browser → it opens there; modifier-click another address, also after restarting Kolux → it opens in the system browser with no dialog.
Fresh profile: press Escape on the dialog → the link opens in the system browser and the dialog does not return.
Fresh profile: turn on the link destination switch on the Terminal & sessions page, then modifier-click an address → it opens in the Kolux browser with no dialog.

cards.title: Shell hooks from different Kolux builds coexist
cards.user_does: Keeps two Kolux builds installed side by side, or moves between an older and a newer version, and opens terminals in each.
cards.user_sees: Terminals in every build start normally, with the user's own shell configuration loaded.
rules: Kolux hooks shell start-up (to know when the prompt is ready and to keep history per worktree) without replacing the user's own start-up files: those still load from the user's own config folder, including a custom zsh config folder the user had set.
Hook files live in Kolux's lasting data folder, not a temporary folder, and are written again if one goes missing while the background host runs.
Each build keeps its hook files where no other build writes (for example a folder named after the files' contents), so a shell never mixes halves from two builds.

Where a folder is shared, files another build left there are kept untouched and are never loaded in place of the user's own files; removing them would make the older build rewrite its hooks over the newer ones and lose the user's config.
acceptance: With two builds installed, open a terminal in each, then a new one in the first again → all start, with the user's own aliases and prompt.

Leave an older build's hook files beside the current ones and let Kolux write its hooks again → the older files are still there unchanged, and a new zsh shell loads the user's config and none of the leftovers.
evidence: registry:unmapped-triage:triage|zsh wrapper dir written by mixed builds
